face, why, long, the

A: I don't know why, but I have a high fever and headache.

A: (B)_________________________________________
B: OK. Than, I'll cook potato soup.
A: Thank you.

<보기>
ⓐ Break a leg.
ⓑ Can I take a rain check?
ⓒ I feel under the weather.
ⓓ It's raining cats and dogs.
ⓔ Chicken soup is not my cup of tea.
questions.explanation: (A) 빈칸 앞에 "What's wrong?"이라는 질문이 있고, A가 "I have a high fever and headache"라고 답했으므로, 상태가 좋지 않다는 표현이 필요하다. "I feel under the weather(ⓒ)"는 "몸이 좋지 않다"는 의미다. (B) B가 "I'll cook chicken soup for you"라고 했는데, A가 그것을 좋아하지 않는다는 표현이 필요하다. "Chicken soup is not my cup of tea(ⓔ)"는 "닭고기 수프는 나의 취향이 아니다"는 뜻이다. 따라서 ⓒ - ⓔ가 정답이다.

questions.question:
위 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

글:
English has often borrowed words from other cultures or languages. Here are some examples with interesting stories.

shampoo
The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, which means "to press." In India, the word was used for a head massage. British traders in India experienced a bath with a head massage and introduced it to Britain in the 18th century.

The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times after it first (A)[entered / entered to] English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.

robot
The word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which was written in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. In the play, robots are machines that look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.

It is interesting that the idea of using the word robot didn't come from Karel Čapek himself. He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." However, his brother suggested roboti, which means "slave workers" in Czech. Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided to use the word roboti. In 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.

hurricane
The word hurricane comes from the Spanish word huracán, which originates from the name of a Mayan god. In the Mayan creation myth, Huracán is the weather god of wind, storm, and fire, and he is one of the three gods (B)[who / whose] created humans. However, the first humans angered the gods, so Huracán (C)[caused / was caused] a great flood.

The first Spanish contact with the Mayan civilization was in 1517. Spanish explorers who were passing through the Caribbean experienced a hurricane and picked up the word for it from the people in the area. In English, one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608.
questions.explanation: (A) "enter English"는 전치사 없이 목적어를 취하므로 "entered"가 맞다. (B) "one of the three gods who created humans"에서 관계대명사 who가 주어 역할을 하므로 "who"가 맞다. (C) "Huracán caused a great flood"에서 Huracán이 주어이므로 능동태 "caused"가 맞다.

He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." (D) Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided to use the word roboti. (E) In 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.
questions.explanation: "However, his brother suggested roboti..."는 Karel Čapek이 원래 labori를 사용하려 했지만, 형이 roboti를 제안했다는 내용이다. 이는 (C)의 "He originally called the machines..."의 설명 이후에 자연스럽게 이어진다. 따라서 (C)와 (D) 사이에 삽입되어야 한다.
